claims.text: - **The $16.8B is solid as a reported figure, but unaudited.** The FT, Reuters (two attendees) and Bloomberg agree on it. Anthropic has not confirmed it on the record, and no public S-1 exists yet. [^1,2,8]
- **"Adjusted" operating profit excludes stock-based compensation but, on the definition used in Anthropic's May projections, includes training costs.**
- **$110B is not Anthropic guidance.** Reuters attributes it to analysts' estimates and the WSJ to investors' expectations. Anthropic gave no September run rate and no full-year outlook. [^2,3]
Reuters' account is the most explicit about its sourcing. It says Q3 revenue "rose to $16.8 billion from $11.6 billion in the second quarter and $4.7 billion in the first quarter"
Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, put Q2 at $11.5 billion and growth at about 46%.
- {term: "Profit metric", def: "Adjusted operating margin of about 11% (Bloomberg: \"11%+\"). Stock-based compensation excluded. No dollar figure. [^3,7]"}
- {term: "Gross margin", def: "Adjusted gross margin of 85%, before training costs. [^7,44]"}
- {term: "Compute efficiency", def: "$1.70 of revenue per $1 of compute in Q3 (FT). [^4]"}

The detail that matters most is the one *not* disclosed. According to The Information, as relayed by The Decoder, some investors were disappointed in part because "the company did not discuss its September annualized revenue rate or a full-year outlook." [^3]
Euronews, citing Bloomberg, goes further and says Anthropic "is now reportedly expected to end 2026 below $100 billion", short of what several backers had anticipated. [^5]
The format also matters, for a legal reason. Anthropic is not an emerging growth company: its 2025 revenue of $4.59 billion exceeds the $1.235 billion threshold.
Reuters' reading of the draft prospectus puts 2025 revenue at $4.59 billion. That is up 1,088% from roughly $386 million in 2024, and it was earned at an operating loss of $8.06 billion. [^9,10]
Bloomberg, citing investor documents in August, reported Q2 2025 revenue of $787 million and Q1 2026 revenue of $4.73 billion. [^18]

The company's own releases put run-rate revenue at about $1 billion at the start of 2025, "over $5 billion" by August 2025, $14 billion on 12 February 2026, more than $30 billion in April, and more than $47 billion in early May. [^13,14,15,16]
Bloomberg then reported more than $19 billion in early March and more than $65 billion at the end of July, citing company investor updates. [^43,17,19]
The FT reported that the Q3 figure fell short of what some of Anthropic's own backers had expected. [^4]
One investor quoted on Techmeme said buy-side expectations had been near $18 billion. [^7]

Take the last 28 days of consumption-billed sales and multiply by 13, then add monthly subscriptions multiplied by 12. [^22] Ed Zitron reports the FT describing the same method from a source "familiar with Anthropic's accounting". [^23]
**The gross-up.** Reuters' reading of the draft prospectus says marketplace sales through Amazon and Google were $2.16 billion, 47% of 2025 revenue.
Anthropic books them gross as principal and records the partners' fees, about $351 million by Reuters' estimate, in the "sales, marketing, and partnerships" operating-expense line. [^12]
The gross-up is real but modest. It is nowhere near the roughly 27% that OpenAI's chief revenue officer alleged in an internal memo.
**The September gap.** In mid-September the New York Times reported, citing four people, that Anthropic would exceed $100 billion in annualized revenue.
Gulf News and Bloomberg render it as "by the end of 2026". Axios, as relayed by Yahoo Finance, wrote that it "is now pacing" above $100 billion, "up 50% from just two months ago." [^20,21]
SemiAnalysis's estimate of about $74 billion, reported by the FT, sits inside that band. [^4,5]
For 2025, Reuters' reading of the draft prospectus reports operating expenses of $12.65 billion against revenue of $4.59 billion, an operating loss of $8.06 billion (2024: $2.98 billion). [^9,10]
The net loss was about $42 billion. Roughly $34 billion of it was a non-cash charge "reflecting a rise in the estimated value of financing that could later turn into Anthropic shares." [^9]
**Exclusion 1: stock-based compensation.** The FT reported in September that Anthropic's adjusted operating income measure "strips out costs including stock-based compensation."
But the WSJ's reading of the May fundraising projections, as reported by PYMNTS, is explicit: "The operating profit figure includes model training costs but excludes stock-based compensation." [^46]
**Exclusion 2: the period.** Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reported the adjusted operating margin as "11%+". The Information, relayed by The Decoder, says the 11% was "for the year through Q3." [^7,3]
In May, Anthropic projected $559 million of operating income for Q2 on $10.9 billion of revenue, and its Q1 compute bill ran 71 cents per revenue dollar. [^46,48]
Anthropic itself told investors in May that it "likely won't be profitable for the whole year" as compute spending rises. [^48,26]
Reuters' reading of the draft prospectus lists at least $518 billion of cloud, compute and infrastructure obligations over roughly a decade.
The largest single line is about $161.2 billion of "Broadcom-related equipment lease obligations that are largely non-cancellable." [^11]
SpaceX's own filing, as reported by Quartz, says "Anthropic will pay $1.25 billion monthly until May 2029," with payments discounted during the May–June ramp. [^26]
The SEC's rule for non-GAAP *liquidity* measures is strict on this point. Item 10(e) bars excluding "charges or liabilities that required, or will require, cash settlement." [^29]

- **Distillation is going away.** Anthropic told investors that distillation traffic was 5% to 7% of revenue, more than $840 million in Q3 by The Information's count, and that it had cut that activity back and expected it to weigh on the current quarter. [^3,4]
- **Price cuts landed in the quarter.** Opus 5.5 launched on 22 September at $4/$20 per million tokens against Opus 5's $5/$25, a 20% list-price cut. [^36]
Anthropic cut Claude Code weekly limits by 17% from 14 September. [^27]
The draft prospectus, as reported by Reuters, says "two customers accounted for nearly one-quarter of its 2025 revenue."
Anthropic has said its growth held "even when you exclude" its two largest customers, and those customers are themselves growing. [^35]
Item 10(e) requires the most directly comparable GAAP measure "with equal or greater prominence" plus a quantitative reconciliation. [^29]

The SEC staff's interpretations narrow what can be adjusted. C&DI 100.01 says a measure can mislead if it excludes "normal, recurring, cash operating expenses necessary to operate a registrant's business."
- {date: "2011-09", headline: "Groupon removes ACSOI", body: "SEC review of its S-1. Groupon told staff that normal marketing dollars are not something it would remove. [^31]"}
Rule 163B makes the investor-day numbers more than marketing. Communications to qualified institutional buyers are "deemed an offer" and carry liability, and SEC staff routinely ask for copies. [^30]

On 25 September the D.C. Circuit ruled 2-1 to uphold the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk, which "bars the military and its contractors from using Anthropic's Claude models." [^39]

The strongest live challenge is the Bloomberg-relayed framing of $110 billion as a "target", which this article treats as a relay error, not a contradiction, because the Reuters and Information accounts say no full-year outlook was given. [^2,3]
